transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that brought you in to see me today?

I keep forgetting everyday things like appointments and errands, and it’s starting to really throw me off. It’s messing up how I take care of my wife and making it hard to keep up with what I’ve promised to do in our neighborhood garden project.
How often do you drink alcohol, and have you or others noticed any changes in your memory or thinking that seem to be worse after drinking or over time with your drinking?

I have a glass of wine with dinner maybe two or three times a week, and that’s about it—never more than one. I haven’t really noticed my memory or focus being worse after I drink, and my family hasn’t said anything about that either.
When did you first start noticing these memory problems, and have they been steadily getting worse, stayed about the same, or come and go depending on stress or life events?

I’ve always been a bit scattered, but things really started getting noticeably worse after my wife’s stroke, when I took over her appointments and paperwork—so a little over a year ago. Since then it feels more tied to how much I have on my plate and how stressed I am, rather than a smooth, steady decline.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling consistently down, hopeless, or very anxious and on edge most days, or is it mainly the forgetfulness and feeling overwhelmed that bothers you?

It’s mainly the forgetfulness and feeling overwhelmed that’s bothering me. I do get tense and worried when I drop the ball, especially about my wife, but I wouldn’t say I feel down or hopeless most days.

Since your wife’s stroke, have there been any major changes in your sleep, appetite, mood, or enjoyment of things you used to like that lasted at least a couple of weeks, or has it mainly been the stress and memory issues without big changes in those areas?

I’d say it’s mostly been the stress and the attention and memory stuff, not big lasting changes in those areas. I still sleep and eat about the same, and I still enjoy the garden and storytelling, just feel more frazzled trying to juggle everything.

Overall, the list has narrowed slightly by removing depressive disorder, but more information is needed to refine further.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that brought you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed prominent attention and everyday memory difficulties after a major psychosocial stressor (wife’s stroke and new caregiving/administrative responsibilities). Symptoms fluctuate with stress load rather than showing a steady neurocognitive decline, and there is no clear pervasive anxiety syndrome or evidence of an organic brain disorder. This pattern is most consistent with an adjustment disorder with predominant disturbance of other emotions/behavior (stress-related cognitive and functional difficulties) rather than a primary anxiety disorder or an organic cognitive syndrome.
